newsitem.title: CHINA: China brokerage Guangfa buys 10 securities units.
newsitem.headline: China brokerage Guangfa buys 10 securities units.

text.p: The Guangfa Securities Co has bought 10 securities units from banks, insurers and rival brokerages to expand its business network, a company official said on Wednesday.
"Through the acquisitions, our business units are now located throughout the country," an official of Guangfa Securities said by telephone from southern Guangzhou, where the brokerage is based.
The brokerage has been trying to expand its business network beyond its base in southern Guangdong province, he said.
The purchases, which started in March 1996, were in line with Beijing's rules ordering banks to sever their ties with securities affiliates, he said.

Securities units that Guangfa had bought had been formerly owned by the Agricultural Bank of China, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, the Guangdong Development Bank, the People's Insurance Company of China.

The company had also bought five units of the failed China Finance Trust and Investment Co that had been taken over by the Guangdong Development Bank, the official said. He declined to say how much Guangfa paid for the 10 securities outlets, in cities such as Beijing, Shanghai, southwestern Chengdu and northeastern Dalian.
Guangfa Securities Co so far has 38 business outlets nationwide, the official said. It has 800 million yuan ($96.4 million) in registered capital and made 260 million yuan in pre-tax profits in 1996.
It is one of three brokerages punished last week by securities authorities for using bank funds to speculate in the stock market.
